cell_type_model: HEK293 cells; human umbilical-vein endothelial cells
assay_or_perturbation: AVP or DDAVP stimulation; beta-arrestin, c-Src, metalloprotease, G-protein and PKA perturbations; vWF secretion assay
relation_type: AVP activates AVPR2/V2R and produces cAMP-linked secretion plus beta-arrestin/c-Src-dependent ERK1/2 activation
pathway_branch: AVPR2 -> Gs/adenylyl cyclase/cAMP-PKA and beta-arrestin-c-Src-MMP transactivation -> ERK1/2 or vWF secretion
limitations: The ERK branch was resolved in HEK293 cells and the vWF output in HUVECs; the studies do not establish a single terminal transcription factor or SCI-specific receiver context.

species: human; structural recombinant complex; human iPSC-derived engineered heart tissue
cell_type_model: BMP10-BMPRII-ALK1 structural complex; BMP10 treatment and receptor-expression/gene-response profiling in engineered heart tissue
assay_or_perturbation: BMP10 receptor-complex evidence supports BMPRII/ALK1, while BMPR1A is only detected or discussed as a possible receptor component in the cardiac model
relation_type: BMP10-BMPR1A pair-specific receptor-complex or relay assignment was not resolved
pathway_branch: BMP10 -> BMPRII/ALK1 or other BMP receptor complexes -> SMAD1/5/8-associated cardiac response; exact BMP10-BMPR1A relay not isolated
limitations: The structural primary study resolves BMPRII and ALK1 rather than BMPR1A; the engineered-heart study reports BMPR1A expression but does not selectively perturb BMPR1A for a BMP10 response. This is a search boundary, not evidence that the pair is inactive.

cell_type_model: KGN human ovarian granulosa cells; mouse pulmonary-artery smooth-muscle cells
assay_or_perturbation: BMP2 stimulation with ActRIIA/ActRIIB/BMPRII siRNA; RGMa expression or knockdown; BMP reporter and alkaline-phosphatase assays
relation_type: BMP2 signaling can use ActRIIA/ACVR2A when an RGM coreceptor changes type-II-receptor utilization; native cells preferentially use BMPRII
pathway_branch: BMP2-RGM/type-II receptor complex -> type-I BMP receptor -> SMAD1/5/8 and BMP reporter or ALP output
limitations: The paper tests ActRIIA as a receptor-complex component and does not support an isolated BMP2-ActRIIA binary molecular edge in every cell type; the effect depends on RGMa and receptor abundance.

cell_type_model: zebrafish gastrula embryos
assay_or_perturbation: bmp2b or bmp2/7 heterodimer overexpression; acvr1l or bmpr1 knockdown; embryonic ventralization and receptor-requirement assays
relation_type: BMP2-family signaling requires an ACVR1-subfamily type-I receptor in the tested embryonic context, including a distinct ACVR1 requirement for overexpressed BMP2 homomer
pathway_branch: BMP2/BMP2-7 -> ACVR1 plus BMPR1-family receptor complex -> SMAD1/5/8-dependent dorsoventral patterning
limitations: The study uses zebrafish Bmp2b and high-expression developmental perturbations; it distinguishes receptor requirement from direct BMP2 homodimer binding to ACVR1 and does not establish a universal mammalian BMP2-ACVR1 complex.

cell_type_model: C2C12 myoblasts; recombinant BMP2 and cell-surface heparan-sulfate perturbation; receptor-assembly and internalization assays
assay_or_perturbation: Cell-surface heparan-sulfate proteoglycans modulate BMP2 sequestration, internalization, and type-II-receptor recruitment, but GPC1 itself was not isolated as the causal proteoglycan
relation_type: HSPG-level BMP2 binding/internalization and receptor-complex modulation without GPC1-specific causal assignment
pathway_branch: BMP2 -> cell-surface HSPG/heparan sulfate -> BMP receptor hetero-oligomerization or internalization -> osteogenic signaling
limitations: These primary studies support an HSPG-level mechanism, not an exact BMP2-GPC1 molecular or intracellular edge; other proteoglycans and glycan composition may account for the effect.

cell_type_model: C2C12 myoblasts; cultured mouse dorsal-root-ganglion explants and neurons
assay_or_perturbation: RGMB/RGMb siRNA or knockout; BMP2 stimulation; BMP reporter, alkaline phosphatase, neurite-outgrowth and rescue assays; ligand-binding measurements
relation_type: RGMB directly binds BMP2 as a GPI-anchored coreceptor and sensitizes BMP2 receptor-complex signaling
pathway_branch: BMP2-RGMB/NEO1-associated coreceptor complex -> type-I/II BMP receptors -> SMAD/BMP response and neurite outgrowth
limitations: The papers establish a coreceptor role and BMP2-dependent functional relay, but the precise stoichiometry and contribution of NEO1 versus other RGM family members are context-dependent.

cell_type_model: human calcitonin-receptor transfectants; primary mouse aortic smooth-muscle and trigeminal-ganglion cultures
assay_or_perturbation: CGRP or calcitonin stimulation; receptor/RAMP1 combination, cAMP accumulation, ligand binding and receptor-isoform assays
relation_type: CALCA-derived CGRP can signal through a CALCR-RAMP1 AMY1 complex, while calcitonin activates CALCR through cAMP and calcium-linked outputs
pathway_branch: CGRP/CALCA -> CALCR-RAMP1 complex -> Gs/cAMP; calcitonin -> CALCR -> cAMP and calcium
limitations: The exact CGRP receptor requires RAMP1 and is not equivalent to isolated CALCR; CALCA encodes a precursor with multiple processed products, and the studies do not identify a terminal TF.

cell_type_model: RAMP1-CALCRL extracellular-domain binding; primary mouse vascular, trigeminal, intestinal lymphatic and enteric models; Calcrl/Ramp1 genetic loss
assay_or_perturbation: CGRP binds and activates the CALCRL/CLR-RAMP1 receptor complex and regulates cAMP-linked vascular or neurolymphatic outputs
relation_type: CGRP-CALCRL/RAMP1 ligand-complex activation and cAMP-linked relay
pathway_branch: CGRP/CALCA -> CALCRL-RAMP1 complex -> Gs/cAMP and tissue-specific vascular, neuronal or lymphatic function
limitations: CALCRL ligand selectivity is imposed by RAMP composition; the pair label omits RAMP1, and the downstream phenotypes are cell-type-specific rather than a single universal relay.

cell_type_model: CHO receptor transfectants; isolated human gallbladder muscle cells; rat nucleus-tractus-solitarius neurons
assay_or_perturbation: CCK-8 stimulation; receptor-selective antagonists; calcium, IP3, PKC, ERK and CREB phosphorylation assays; intracerebral MEK inhibition
relation_type: CCK activates CCKAR through Gq-linked calcium/IP3-PKC signaling and can engage ERK-CREB in the NTS satiety circuit
pathway_branch: CCK -> CCKAR -> Gq/IP3-Ca2+/PKC and ERK -> CREB phosphorylation or gallbladder contraction/satiety output
limitations: CCK receptor coupling differs by cell type and ligand concentration; the NTS study uses systemic CCK and receptor localization rather than a purified receptor-only reconstruction.

cell_type_model: CHO cells expressing CCKBR; NIH/3T3 cells expressing wild-type or truncated CCKBR
assay_or_perturbation: CCK-8-S stimulation; calcium and cAMP assays; receptor truncation and internalization measurements
relation_type: CCK activates CCKBR with calcium mobilization; CCKBR carboxyl-terminal phosphorylation sites regulate ligand-induced internalization
pathway_branch: CCK -> CCKBR -> Gq/Ca2+ signaling and PKC-sensitive desensitization/internalization
limitations: The cited comparison found robust calcium coupling for CCKBR but not the CCKAR-like cAMP response; internalization is receptor trafficking rather than a terminal transcriptional pathway.

cell_type_model: THP-1 monocytes; CCR2b and CCR3 transfectants
assay_or_perturbation: radioligand binding; CCR2/CCR3 transfectant chemotaxis; intracellular calcium flux; receptor antagonism and MCP-1 competition
relation_type: CCL11/eotaxin is a low-potency partial agonist and ligand of CCR2b in addition to its stronger CCR3 activity
pathway_branch: CCL11 -> CCR2b -> chemokine GPCR calcium/chemotaxis branch, with partial agonism and competition against MCP-1
limitations: The CCR2 effect occurs at high CCL11 concentrations and is weaker than canonical CCL11-CCR3 signaling; it should not be generalized across species or receptor isoforms.

cell_type_model: CXCR3 transfectants; human eosinophils and CCR3 transfectants
assay_or_perturbation: CCL11 binding and receptor-response assays; receptor chimeras; chemotaxis and cross-inhibition assays
relation_type: CCL11 binds CXCR3 but does not activate it in the tested system, consistent with a decoy/sequestration role
pathway_branch: CCL11 -> CXCR3 binding/decoy branch -> altered local chemokine availability and indirect regulation of CCR3 responses
limitations: The study explicitly reports no CXCR3 agonism; no intracellular CXCR3 relay should be materialized for this pair, and the binding may depend on receptor expression and local chemokine competition.

cell_type_model: mouse blood, spleen, bone-marrow and pulmonary leukocytes; ACKR2-deficient mice
assay_or_perturbation: fluorescent CCL2/CCL12 uptake and competition; Ackr2 knockout; leukocyte migration and metastatic models
relation_type: ACKR2 participates in atypical chemokine scavenging and CCL12 competition, constraining conventional chemokine-receptor activity rather than coupling as a classical G-protein relay
pathway_branch: CCL12 -> ACKR2 scavenging/internalization -> chemokine-gradient control and secondary CCR2/NK-cell migratory effects
limitations: ACKR2 is atypical and generally does not produce a canonical G-protein signal; the studies use CCL12 competition and scavenging contexts, so no direct CCL12-ACKR2 TF pathway is inferred.

cell_type_model: CCR8-transfected liposomes and HEK293/Jurkat receptor systems; mouse and human immune-cell models
assay_or_perturbation: SPR, saturation and competition binding; proximity ligation; ligand-induced receptor signaling and in vivo immune perturbation
relation_type: CCL17 binds CCR8 with high affinity and activates a noncanonical CCR8 Gi-linked signaling axis in the tested inflammatory context
pathway_branch: CCL17 -> CCR8 -> Gi-linked chemokine signaling -> CCL3/T-cell regulatory and atherosclerotic inflammatory outputs
limitations: The paper describes a noncanonical/context-dependent CCL17-CCR8 axis and broader immune phenotypes; the precise downstream transcription factor is not established for this exact pair.

cell_type_model: CCR1 peptide/receptor binding systems; CHO cells expressing CCR1 or CCR5
assay_or_perturbation: chemokine-peptide competition/binding; receptor-transfectant calcium-flux and chemotaxis assays
relation_type: CCL2 participates in CCR1 binding-site comparisons, but the strongest functional CCR1 evidence in the cited panel is for other CC chemokines
pathway_branch: CCL2 -> CCR1 N-terminal/receptor-contact boundary -> possible chemokine-receptor competition; no pair-specific relay promoted
limitations: CCL2 is canonical for CCR2, and the evidence here does not establish a robust full-length CCL2-CCR1 signaling response; do not transfer CCR1 signaling from CCL3/CCL5 or other chemokines.

cell_type_model: ACKR4-expressing cells and fluorescent-chemokine uptake systems
assay_or_perturbation: fluorescent CCL20 uptake; beta-arrestin1/2 recruitment; cross-species chemokine comparison
relation_type: CCL20 is taken up by ACKR4, which recruits beta-arrestin and functions primarily as a scavenging atypical chemokine receptor
pathway_branch: CCL20 -> ACKR4 -> beta-arrestin-biased internalization/scavenging -> chemokine-gradient regulation
limitations: The mouse CCL20 response is species-dependent and weaker at human ACKR4 in some assays; ACKR4 does not provide a canonical G-protein pathway or validated terminal TF endpoint.

cell_type_model: CHO cells expressing CCR1 or CCR5; primary or activated human lymphocyte-derived chemokine preparations
assay_or_perturbation: CCL4/MIP-1beta receptor-transfectant calcium and chemotaxis assays; native N-terminal truncation and receptor-specificity comparison
relation_type: Native or naturally truncated CCL4 can engage CCR1, with N-terminal processing changing receptor specificity and enabling CCR1 calcium signaling
pathway_branch: CCL4 -> CCR1 -> chemokine GPCR calcium/chemotaxis branch, strongest for the naturally truncated CCL4(3-69) form
limitations: Full-length CCL4 is more strongly associated with CCR5; the CCR1 activity is processing-dependent and should not be treated as a uniform CCL4-CCR1 response across preparations.

cell_type_model: SH-SY5Y human neuroblastoma cells; primary rat cortical neurons; recombinant GPR75-transfected cells
assay_or_perturbation: CCL5 stimulation; GPR75 CRISPR knockdown; AKT/GSK3beta/ERK phosphorylation, calcium/IP-1 and internalization assays; SPR and receptor antagonists
relation_type: CCL5 activates or modulates GPR75 in a context-dependent manner, with GPR75-dependent ERK/AKT signaling in neuronal cells and low-affinity binding without direct activation in a 20-HETE system
pathway_branch: CCL5 -> GPR75 -> PLC/Gq-linked or PTX-independent AKT-ERK signaling -> neuronal survival-related output
limitations: The two primary studies disagree on whether CCL5 is an agonist versus a low-affinity negative regulator, likely reflecting assay and receptor-context differences; no terminal TF was directly measured.

cell_type_model: primary human endothelial/angiogenic cell systems and syndecan/glycosaminoglycan perturbation models
assay_or_perturbation: CCL5/RANTES stimulation; syndecan-1 and syndecan-4 manipulation; angiogenesis and cell-signaling readouts
relation_type: CCL5 associates with cell-surface glycosaminoglycan-bearing syndecans including SDC1, but the cited evidence does not isolate a unique SDC1 intracellular relay
pathway_branch: CCL5 -> SDC1-associated glycosaminoglycan presentation -> local chemokine retention and angiogenic context
limitations: Syndecans are proteoglycan presentation/adhesion components rather than canonical chemokine GPCRs; the study emphasizes SDC4/PKCalpha for signaling and does not establish a direct SDC1 kinase cascade.

cell_type_model: primary human endothelial/angiogenic cell systems and syndecan-4 perturbation models
assay_or_perturbation: CCL5/RANTES treatment; SDC4 knockdown or interference; PKCalpha pathway and proangiogenic functional assays
relation_type: CCL5-dependent proangiogenic signaling requires a syndecan-4/PKCalpha branch in addition to CCR1, consistent with SDC4 acting as a cell-surface presentation/signaling component
pathway_branch: CCL5 -> SDC4-associated proteoglycan/PKCalpha branch plus CCR1 -> proangiogenic migration and tube-formation outputs
limitations: The paper does not define a direct protein-protein CCL5-SDC4 interface or a SDC4-only pathway; heparan-sulfate presentation and CCR1 co-signaling are required context.

cell_type_model: CD177-positive neutrophils; HUVECs; glomerular endothelial-cell injury models
assay_or_perturbation: CD177-Fc or PECAM1 treatment; adhesion, transendothelial migration, SHP-1/PECAM1 phosphorylation, integrin, ERK, degranulation and endothelial-injury assays
relation_type: CD177 is a heterophilic PECAM1 counter-receptor; engagement changes PECAM1/SHP-1 and integrin-ERK signaling and modulates neutrophil activation or transmigration
pathway_branch: CD177-PECAM1 adhesion/signaling complex -> PECAM1/SHP-1 and beta2-integrin-Src-ERK branches -> neutrophil migration/degranulation outputs
limitations: CD177 is GPI-anchored and lacks a cytosolic domain, so signaling is mediated by PECAM1 and associated integrins; directionality and endothelial allele effects are context-dependent.

cell_type_model: mouse and human myeloid cells; pulmonary ILC2s; stroke and lung-inflammation models
assay_or_perturbation: CD200-Fc or CD200 engagement; CD200R1 knockout/blockade; NF-kappaB, cytokine, cell-activation and inflammatory phenotyping
relation_type: CD200 binds CD200R1 and transmits an inhibitory immune-regulatory signal that suppresses activation and canonical/noncanonical NF-kappaB outputs
pathway_branch: CD200-CD200R1 -> Dok2/adapter-linked inhibitory signaling -> reduced NF-kappaB and inflammatory cytokine or leukocyte-activation output
limitations: The receptor family includes closely related CD200R-like proteins with species-specific expression; the cited studies validate pathway function but do not identify a single terminal TF.

cell_type_model: mouse bone-marrow-derived dendritic-cell and CD200-receptor-family models
assay_or_perturbation: CD200-Fc or CD200 overexpression in CD200R1-deficient mice; agonist antibody to CD200R2; dendritic-cell differentiation and T-regulatory-cell assays
relation_type: CD200R2-family engagement is associated with altered dendritic-cell differentiation, but direct CD200-to-CD200R2 binding and a defined intracellular relay are not resolved
pathway_branch: CD200/CD200R-family engagement -> altered myeloid/DC program -> T-regulatory-cell and alloreactivity outputs
limitations: Mouse CD200R paralogs are difficult to map one-to-one to human receptor nomenclature; CD200 stimulation in CD200R1-deficient settings is not sufficient to prove a direct CD200R2 molecular edge.

cell_type_model: mouse and human myeloid cells; pulmonary ILC2s; stroke and lung-inflammation models
assay_or_perturbation: CD200-Fc or CD200 engagement; CD200R1 knockout/blockade; NF-kappaB, cytokine, cell-activation and inflammatory phenotyping
relation_type: CD200R1 is the inhibitory receptor component that engages CD200 and transduces the same immune-regulatory branch represented by the reverse submitted orientation
pathway_branch: CD200R1 receptor -> CD200 counter-ligand -> Dok2/adapter-linked inhibitory signaling -> reduced NF-kappaB and inflammatory output
limitations: The submitted orientation is retained exactly; the biological receptor-ligand direction is CD200R1 receptor with CD200 counter-ligand. No separate reverse biochemical interaction is inferred.

cell_type_model: mouse B cells and CD45-deficient or ST6Gal1-deficient lymphocytes; BCR-ligated B-cell models
assay_or_perturbation: CD22 ligand-binding and redistribution assays; CD45 or glycosylation loss; BCR ligation; SHP-1 and CD22 phosphorylation measurements
relation_type: CD22 recognizes alpha2,6-sialylated cis/trans ligands including CD45 in a context-dependent manner, influencing CD22 clustering and SHP-1-mediated BCR regulation
pathway_branch: CD22-sialylated-CD45/glycoconjugate context -> CD22 ITIM/SHP-1 branch -> modulation of BCR signaling
limitations: The interaction is glycan-dependent and CD45 is not required for all CD22 redistribution assays; evidence supports a context-dependent ligand/co-receptor role, not a universal direct CD22-PTPRC protein-protein edge or terminal TF.
